title: Blood Amber Figurine of a Child Riding a Sheep
description:
Unearthed in 2015 from a Cao Wei royal tomb in Luoyang, believed to be that of Princess Pingyuan (Cao Shu), the beloved daughter of Emperor Ming of Wei (Cao Rui). 

The figurine depicts a child riding a sheep while grasping its horns. Such motifs often symbolised transcendence and immortality, expressing hopes for the deceased's ascension. 

A stone plaque inscribed "Plain-Carved Child Riding a Sheep No.1" was also found in the tomb. Here, "plain-carved" refers to an undecorated surface incised with simple lines.
description_zh_hant:
此件騎羊俑出土於洛陽西朱村曹魏大墓，墓主推測為屬魏明帝愛女平原公主曹淑。俑作童子狀，雙手緊握羊角，穩坐羊背，姿態生動。此類騎羊形象往往象徵得道昇仙之寓意，寄託對亡靈登仙的祝願。

墓中亦出土刻有「白畫騎羊兒一」六字石牌，「白畫」即素面刻紋之意。
description_zh_hans:
此件骑羊俑出土于洛阳西朱村曹魏大墓，墓主推测为属魏明帝爱女平原公主曹淑。俑作童子状，双手紧握羊角，稳坐羊背，姿态生动。此类骑羊形象往往象征得道升仙之寓意，寄托对亡灵登仙的祝愿。

墓中亦出土刻有「白画骑羊儿一」六字石牌，「白画」即素面刻纹之意。

title: Seal Impression of the Grand Administrator of Shu
description:
A seal impression is the surviving remnant of the ancient sealing practice. Official documents were written on bamboo or wooden slips, tied together with cord, then sealed by pressing clay over the knot and stamping it with an official seal. To read the document, the impression had to be broken, making any tampering immediately apparent.

As paper gradually replaced bamboo and wooden slips as the primary writing material, this method of sealing gradually fell out of use. This example bears the inscription "Seal of the Grand Administrator of Shu Commandery."
description_zh_hant:
封泥是古代使用印章的實物遺存。古人將文書寫於竹木簡上，以繩捆紮，並在打結處填泥蓋印，形成封泥。若要開啟閱讀，必須先破壞封泥，因此封泥一旦有損，就代表文件可能被私自拆閱。

隨著紙張取代簡牘成為主要書寫材料，封泥也逐漸退出歷史舞臺。
description_zh_hans:
封泥是古代使用印章的实物遗存。古人将文书写于竹木简上，以绳捆扎，并在打结处填泥盖印，形成封泥。若要开启阅读，必须先破坏封泥，因此封泥一旦有损，就代表文件可能被私自拆阅。

随着纸张取代简牍成为主要书写材料，封泥也逐渐退出历史舞台。

title: Xue Qiu's Wooden Name Plaque
description:
This name plaque was unearthed from a Three Kingdoms tomb discovered in Nanjing. The tomb is believed to belong to Xue Qiu, who may have been a member of the same clan as the prominent Wu statesman Xue Zong. Name plaques served as calling cards during life and were also buried with the deceased for use in the afterlife.

The left plaque records Xue Qiu's details like place of origin, name and rank. Such plaques likely served as identification for the deceased in the underworld, reflecting the belief that the dead continued to require the same care and formalities as the living.
description_zh_hant:
這枚名刺出土於南京一處工地發現的墓葬，隨葬品特徵顯示其年代屬三國東吳時期，墓主薛秋可能與東吳名臣薛綜同宗。名刺在當時既用於生前交際，亦隨葬以供死後所用。

左側名刺刻有「折鋒校尉沛國竹邑東鄉安平里公乘薛秋年六十六字子春」，詳列籍貫、姓名、字號、官爵與年齡。此類名刺應為向陰間官府通報之憑證，生動體現了「事死如事生」的喪葬觀念。
description_zh_hans:
这枚名刺出土于南京一处工地发现的墓葬，随葬品特征显示其年代属三国东吴时期，墓主薛秋可能与东吴名臣薛综同宗。名刺在当时既用于生前交际，亦随葬以供死后所用。

左侧名刺刻有「折锋校尉沛国竹邑东乡安平里公乘薛秋年六十六字子春」，详列籍贯、姓名、字号、官爵与年龄。此类名刺应为向阴间官府通报之凭证，生动体现了「事死如事生」的丧葬观念。

title: Tiger Tally of Du
description:
This bronze military tally from the Warring States period is the left half of a tiger tally, cast in the form of a striding tiger with its head held high. Its surface bears a 40-character inscription in small seal script, inlaid using the gold-inlay technique.

The inscription states that the left half was entrusted to the commander at Du, while the matching half was retained by the ruler to verify military orders before troops could be mobilised.
description_zh_hant: 這枚戰國時期的青銅兵符是虎符的左半部分，造型為一隻昂首闊步的猛虎，為杜地長官所持。虎符表面以錯金工藝鐫刻著9行共40字的小篆銘文，內容明確規定了兵符的使用規章，反映出當時其高度集中的軍事指揮體系。
description_zh_hans: 这枚战国时期的青铜兵符是虎符的左半部分，造型为一只昂首阔步的猛虎，为杜地长官所持。虎符表面以错金工艺镌刻着9行共40字的小篆铭文，内容明确规定了兵符的使用规章，反映出当时其高度集中的军事指挥体系。

title: Zhibai Wuzhu Coin
description:
The Zhibai Wuzhu was a coin minted by Shu Han during the Three Kingdoms period. Round with a square central hole, its inscription is arranged in the order top, bottom, right, then left. 

The characters Zhibai are written in clerical script, while Wuzhu is in small seal script.Here, zhi (直) is a phonetic loan for zhi (值, "value"), while Wuzhu refers to the standard Han-dynasty coin. Thus, Zhibai Wuzhu literally means "Wuzhu worth one hundred." 

Modern archaeological finds have yielded far more Shu coins than those of Wei and Wu, and historical records show that the Zhibai Wuzhu remained in circulation into the Liang dynasty (502-557), more than two centuries after its introduction.
description_zh_hant:
直百五銖乃三國時期蜀漢政權所鑄造的重要貨幣。此錢外圓內方，錢文以「上、下、右、左」的方式排列，其中「直百」二字為隸書，「五銖」為小篆。「直」字為「值」之通假，「五銖」本為漢代貨幣，故「直百五銖」之意即幣值百元的五銖。

從考古發現來看，蜀漢鑄幣在數量上均遠超同期魏、吳兩國，且影響甚廣，直至兩百多年后的南朝梁武帝時仍在民間流通。
description_zh_hans:
直百五铢乃三国时期蜀汉政权所铸造的重要货币。此钱外圆内方，钱文以「上、下、右、左」的方式排列，其中「直百」二字为隶书，「五铢」为小篆。「直」字为「值」之通假，「五铢」本为汉代货币，故「直百五铢」之意即币值百元的五铢。

从考古发现来看，蜀汉铸币在数量上均远超同期魏、吴两国，且影响甚广，直至两百多年后的南朝梁武帝时仍在民间流通。

title: Tang Sancai Camel
description:
This camel figurine was unearthed from the joint tomb of General An Pu and his wife in the southern suburbs of Luoyang. A Sogdian by origin, An Pu was born in the Western Regions, died in Chang'an, and was buried in Luoyang. 

The camel is vividly modelled, with its head held high and mouth open in a braying cry. Its back is adorned with a finely patterned carpet and travelling gear, including saddlebags decorated with beast-mask motifs. 

A fine example of Tang sancai, or "Tang three-colour ware," it is glazed in white, green, and brown, reflecting both the technical sophistication of Tang ceramics and the flourishing trade and cultural exchange along the Silk Road.
description_zh_hant:
這件駱駝俑出土於洛陽南郊的定遠將軍安菩夫婦合葬墓。墓主人安菩作為一個粟特人，生於西域，死於長安，葬於洛陽，人生軌跡極富傳奇色彩。

駱駝俑造型生動傳神：頭部高昂，張口嘶鳴；背部裝飾考究，鋪有精美花毯，並有獸面紋馱囊等行裝。

作為典型的唐三彩作品，此俑以白、綠、褐三色釉彩交織渲染，色澤斑斕絢麗。它不僅展現了唐代三彩工藝的高超水準，更是當時絲綢之路商貿繁榮與文化交融的真實寫照。
description_zh_hans:
这件骆驼俑出土于洛阳南郊的定远将军安菩夫妇合葬墓。墓主人安菩作为一个粟特人，生于西域，死于长安，葬于洛阳，人生轨迹极富传奇色彩。

骆驼俑造型生动传神：头部高昂，张口嘶鸣；背部装饰考究，铺有精美花毯，并有兽面纹驮囊等行装。

作为典型的唐三彩作品，此俑以白、绿、褐三色釉彩交织渲染，色泽斑斓绚丽。它不仅展现了唐代三彩工艺的高超水准，更是当时丝绸之路商贸繁荣与文化交融的真实写照。

title: The Multi-faced Seal of Dugu Xin
description:
This seal belonged to Dugu Xin, a Xianbei noble and one of the Eight Pillar-Generals of Western Wei. Carved from jet stone, the seal is composed of 26 square and triangular faces of varying sizes. Among them, 14 square faces bear engraved inscriptions.

The inscriptions fall into three categories: (1) for issuing official documents, (2) for submitting memorials to the emperor, and (3) for private correspondence. The seal's unique design makes it a distinctive and exceptional example among all ancient seals known to date.
description_zh_hant:
這枚印章屬於西魏八柱國之一的鮮卑貴族獨孤信。印章以煤精石為材，由26個大小各異的正方形與三角形構成，其中14個正方形印面鐫刻有不同印文。

其印文內容可分為三類：一為簽發公文之用，二為上奏皇帝之用，三為私人書信之用。此印形制獨特，在迄今所見的古代印章中實屬罕見。
description_zh_hans:
这枚印章属于西魏八柱国之一的鲜卑贵族独孤信。印章以煤精石为材，由26个大小各异的正方形与三角形构成，其中14个正方形印面镌刻有不同印文。

其印文内容可分为三类：一为签发公文之用，二为上奏皇帝之用，三为私人书信之用。此印形制独特，在迄今所见的古代印章中实属罕见。

title: Celadon Tiger Vessel
description:
The Tiger Vessel takes its name from its tiger-like form. Originating during the Warring States period, it became widespread from the Han dynasty through the Six Dynasties.

Celadon vesselswere common burial objects during this period, typically modelled with a tiger's head raised to form the spout and an arched handle across the back. Scholars remain divided over their intended function, with some identifying them as water vessels and others as chamber pots.
description_zh_hant:
虎子源起於戰國，盛行於漢代至六朝，因其器形肖似虎狀而得名。青瓷虎子是六朝墓葬中常見的隨葬品，多作仰首之態，以虎首為口，并在虎背設有拱形提梁作爲把手。

關於青瓷虎子的用途，學界存在盛水與尿壺兩種觀點，尚無定論。
description_zh_hans:
虎子源起于战国，盛行于汉代至六朝，因其器形肖似虎状而得名。青瓷虎子是六朝墓葬中常见的随葬品，多作仰首之态，以虎首为口，并在虎背设有拱形提梁作为把手。

关于青瓷虎子的用途，学界存在盛水与尿壶两种观点，尚无定论。

title: Jade Burial Suit of Jiangdu
description:
This jade burial suit was unearthed from the tomb of Liu Fei, Prince of Jiangdu, the son of Emperor Jing of Han and elder half-brother to Emperor Wu. The suit is composed of more than two thousand jade plaques meticulously strung together, a process that would have taken several years to complete.

During the Han dynasty, it was believed that encasing the deceased in enduring materials such as jade can preserve the body and its vital qi, enabling one to attain immortality. Today, the jade burial suits displayed in museums may, in a symbolic sense, have fulfilled their owners' aspirations for eternal life.
description_zh_hant:
這件金縷玉衣出土於江都王劉非的墓葬中。劉非是漢景帝劉啟之子，也是漢武帝劉徹同父異母的兄長，曾參與平定著名的「七國之亂」。

整件玉衣由兩千餘片玉片編綴，需耗時數年方可完成。漢代盛行神仙思想，時人普遍相信，若死後肉身不腐，保住體內之「氣」，便可登仙永生。而實現肉身不朽的最佳方式，正是以金玉這類亙古不壞的材質嚴密包裹遺體。

如今，陳列於博物館中的金縷玉衣，或許真的以某種形式，完成了主人不朽的心願。
description_zh_hans:
这件金缕玉衣出土于江都王刘非的墓葬中。刘非是汉景帝刘启之子，也是汉武帝刘彻同父异母的兄长，曾参与平定著名的「七国之乱」。

整件玉衣由两千余片玉片编缀，需耗时数年方可完成。汉代盛行神仙思想，时人普遍相信，若死后肉身不腐，保住体内之「气」，便可登仙永生。而实现肉身不朽的最佳方式，正是以金玉这类亘古不坏的材质严密包裹遗体。

如今，陈列于博物馆中的金缕玉衣，或许真的以某种形式，完成了主人不朽的心愿。

title: Cao Quan Stele
description:
The Cao Quan Stele, formally titled The Stele of Cao Quan, Magistrate of Heyang, was carved in the second year of the Zhongping era (185 CE) during the Eastern Han dynasty and unearthed in Heyang County, Shaanxi, during the Wanli reign of the Ming dynasty. The inscription records the lineage, life, and official achievements of Cao Quan, including his suppression of the Yellow Turban Rebellion.

The main inscription comprises 1165 characters. Renowned for its graceful, flowing style, it has long been regarded as one of the finest examples of clerical script and remains one of the most celebrated Han steles.
description_zh_hant:
《曹全碑》，全称《汉郃阳令曹全碑》，刻于东汉中平二年，明万历年间出土于陕西郃阳县。碑文详载郃阳令曹全之家世、生平与政绩，其中包括其镇压黄巾起事之事。

碑文共1165字，书法秀逸舒展、翩然有致，历来为隶书学习之经典范本，在汉碑中久负盛名。

title: White Jade Cup
description:
This white jade cup was unearthed from a Cao Wei tomb in Luoyang. Although the tomb had been looted and most of its grave goods lost, the cup survived intact.An inscription reading "Eighth Year of Zhengshi, Eighth Month," carved on iron curtain-frame components from the tomb, dates the burial to the reign of Cao Fang. 

Carved from a single piece of lustrous white jade, the cup is entirely undecorated, relying instead on the natural beauty and purity of the material to embody the aesthetic ideal of "beauty inherent in nature."
dimensions: Approx. 13 cm high; 5 cm mouth diameter
description_zh_hant:
此尊白玉杯出土于洛阳一座曹魏墓。该墓曾遭盗掘，随葬品多已散佚，唯此玉杯完好无损，幸免于难。

墓内铁帷帐构件上刻有「正始八年八月」铭文，据此确知墓葬年代为魏齐王芳时期。玉杯通体以晶莹白玉雕琢而成，光素无纹，却以温润纯净之质，尽显「美在天然」的至高意趣。

title: Tiger-Motif Bronze Dagger-Axe
description:
The rear of this bronze dagger-axe is decorated on both sides with half-relief tiger heads, their jaws agape, while incised lines behind them depict the tigers' bodies. Bashu symbols also appear on parts of the blade. Tiger motifs are among the most common decorative themes on Bashu bronzes, often occupying prominent positions on the vessel or weapon.

This echoes the Book of the Later Han, which records the Ba people's veneration of the tiger. Comparable tiger-decorated weapons have also been unearthed in Chongqing and elsewhere in the Bashu region.
dimensions: Approx. 25 x 14 x 2 cm (L x W x Thickness)
description_zh_hant:
此铜戈后部两面均饰半浮雕虎首，虎口大张，其后阴刻虎身，局部并见巴蜀符号。虎纹为巴蜀文化青铜器中最常见的主题纹饰之一，多置于器物显著位置，与《后汉书》所载巴人崇虎之俗相合。

同类虎纹兵器在重庆等地亦多有出土。

title: Silver Ewer with Dancing Horses
description:
The Silver Ewer with Dancing Horses has a flattened, rounded body modelled after the leather flasks of the northern nomadic peoples, reflecting the cultural diversity of the Tang dynasty. Its surface is engraved with two dancing horses, kneeling with cups in their mouths, vividly depicting the court performance held in celebration of Emperor Xuanzong's birthday.

Following the An Lushan Rebellion, Xuanzong fled the capital, the dancing horses were dispersed, and the once-fashionable performance disappeared. The ewer thus stands as a poignant witness to both the splendour and decline of the Tang dynasty.
description_zh_hant:
舞馬銜杯紋銀壺器身扁圓，造型仿自北方游牧民族之皮囊壺，體現了當時不同民族間的文化交融。壺身鏨刻兩匹舞馬，奮首鼓尾，銜杯跪拜，生動再現了唐代詩文所載宮廷舞馬「屈膝銜杯」、為玄宗祝壽之景。

安史亂起，玄宗倉皇西奔，舞馬流散，盛極一時的舞馬祝壽遂告絕跡。此壺亦由此成為唐朝盛衰之際的獨特見證。
description_zh_hans:
舞马衔杯纹银壶器身扁圆，造型仿自北方游牧民族之皮囊壶，体现了当时不同民族间的文化交融。壶身錾刻两匹舞马，奋首鼓尾，衔杯跪拜，生动再现了唐代诗文所载宫廷舞马「屈膝衔杯」、为玄宗祝寿之景。

安史乱起，玄宗仓皇西奔，舞马流散，盛极一时的舞马祝寿遂告绝迹。此壶亦由此成为唐朝盛衰之际的独特见证。
